correctness.rationale: The graph is the induced cyclic no-adjacent-ones word graph, with closed Hamming-radius-one neighborhoods. For a given sensor set, intersecting each closed neighborhood and each pairwise symmetric difference is exactly the nonempty and distinct signature condition. It is upward closed, so excluding the entire layer of size I_n−1 excludes every smaller code. The independent exhaustive boundary-layer replay (independent_lucas_audit.py and witness_run.txt under /workspace/branches/dff87c4d-ce95-452d-bdb5-d831732613b7) tested all 20,030,010 ten-subsets and 34,597,290 eleven-subsets at n=7, giving zero and 259. A second independent search /workspace/evidence/lucas.py (outputs lucas-2-6.txt and lucas-7.txt) found the same results with disjoint branching: remove redundant superset constraints, split completions by the first selected available vertex in an unhit constraint, and when no constraints remain enumerate every exact-size completion. It certifies every cardinality through each optimum and directly verifies signatures for accepted codes. Both reconstruct the coordinate action and enumerate the code orbits and every union of vertex orbits. All rows agree: unrestricted minima 2,3,4,5,7,11, counts 1,4,13,21,18,259; invariant minima 2,3,4,5,8,14, counts 1,1,1,1,1,3. At n=6 the unique invariant optimum is the six singletons and the two alternating words. At n=7 there are nine optimum orbits of size 7 and fourteen of size 14; exactly three optimal invariant unions, each the weight-one orbit plus the orbit of 0000101, 0001001 or 0010101. The explicit unrestricted witness also passes direct signature testing. Repeated representatives at n=2 do not affect orbits. Therefore 6 is the first dimension in the stated range (and among n≥2) with a penalty, and the penalty at 7 is three. No extrapolation beyond 7.

evidence: Fibonacci record 529792b7a045 has a linear adjacency constraint on coordinates and reversal invariance, whereas the Lucas cube also forbids wrap-around consecutive ones and uses all dihedral symmetries. Mollard treats perfect codes, where radius-one balls partition the vertex set.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Removing words changes all relevant neighborhood signatures; Fibonacci minima, counts, and reversal-only constraints do not transfer. Perfect codes enforce exactly one codeword in each ball, with repeated signatures for vertices in the same nontrivial ball; that is not identification.

value.rationale: The cyclic cube and full coordinate symmetry define a natural constraint on identifying placements. The finite cutoff contains the first strict symmetry penalty and the next case where it increases, and explains the equality cases and the difference between labelled codes, code orbits and invariant codes. These exact small benchmarks and explicit placements are meaningful without implying a growth law or an asymptotic threshold.
